Red Pozole

Served at: Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe

Serves 8-10Prep 45 minCook 3 hours

Red Pozole, or Pozole Rojo, is a hearty and flavorful Mexican stew traditionally made with hominy and pork, simmered in a rich, red chile broth. It is a beloved dish often prepared for special occasions and holidays, including the Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe on December 12th, where families gather to celebrate with traditional foods that nourish both body and spirit.

Ingredients

  • 3 pounds (1.4 kg) pork shoulder (Boston butt), cut into 2-inch (5 cm) cubes
  • 1 large white onion, halved
  • 6 cloves garlic, peeled
  • 2 bay leaves
  • 1 teaspoon (5 g) dried oregano, preferably Mexican
  • 1 teaspoon (5 g) ground cumin
  • Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
  • 12 cups (2.8 liters) water or chicken broth
  • 3 (15-ounce / 425 g) cans white hominy, drained and rinsed
  • 8 dried Guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded
  • 3 dried Ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
  • 3-5 dried Chile de Arbol (optional, for heat), stemmed and seeded
  • For serving:
  • Shredded green cabbage
  • Sliced radishes
  • Diced white onion
  • Chopped fresh cilantro
  • Lime wedges
  • Tostadas or tortilla chips

Method

  1. Place the pork shoulder in a large pot or Dutch oven. Add one half of the white onion, 3 cloves of garlic, bay leaves, 1/2 teaspoon (2.5 g) oregano, 1/2 teaspoon (2.5 g) cumin, 1 tablespoon (15 g) salt, and 1/2 teaspoon (2.5 g) black pepper.
  2. Pour in 12 cups (2.8 liters) of water or chicken broth, ensuring the pork is fully submerged. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until the pork is tender and easily shredded.
  3. While the pork simmers, prepare the chile sauce. In a separate saucepan, combine the dried Guajillo, Ancho, and Arbol chiles. Cover with water and bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer for 10-15 minutes, until the chiles are softened.
  4. Carefully transfer the softened chiles to a blender. Add the remaining half of the white onion, 3 cloves of garlic, 1/2 teaspoon (2.5 g) oregano, 1/2 teaspoon (2.5 g) cumin, and 1 cup (240 ml) of the chile soaking liquid (or fresh water). Blend until completely smooth, adding more liquid if needed to achieve a pourable consistency.
  5. Once the pork is tender, remove it from the pot and shred it using two forks. Discard the onion half, garlic cloves, and bay leaves from the cooking liquid. Strain the cooking liquid through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean bowl, discarding any solids. This is your pork broth.
  6. Return the shredded pork to the cleaned pot. Add the drained and rinsed hominy. Pour the blended chile sauce through a fine-mesh sieve directly into the pot with the pork and hominy, pressing on the solids to extract all the liquid. Discard the remaining pulp.
  7. Add the strained pork broth back into the pot. Stir everything together. Bring the pozole to a gentle simmer over medium-low heat. Cook for another 30-45 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the hominy to fully absorb the broth. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
  8. Serve the Red Pozole hot in large bowls. Offer a variety of garnishes on the side, such as shredded cabbage, sliced radishes, diced white onion, chopped cilantro, and lime wedges, allowing each person to customize their bowl. Serve with tostadas or tortilla chips for dipping.

Tips

  • For a richer flavor, toast the dried chiles lightly in a dry skillet for 1-2 minutes before soaking. Be careful not to burn them, as this can make the sauce bitter.
  • If you prefer a spicier pozole, you can add more Chile de Arbol or a pinch of cayenne pepper to the chile sauce.
  • Pozole tastes even better the next day! Make it ahead of time and gently reheat on the stovetop, adding a little water or broth if it has thickened too much.
